findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_form144_notices, get_eu_major_holdings · Private data: list_institutions, get_insider_trades, search, sec_get_filing_index, sec_get_filing_document · Public sink: get_institution_holdings, get_stock_activity, get_insider_trades, get_form144_notices, get_ftd_data, get_gov_contracts.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_form144_notices, get_eu_major_holdings · Private data: list_institutions, get_insider_trades, search, sec_get_filing_index, sec_get_filing_document · Public sink: get_institution_holdings, get_stock_activity, get_insider_trades, get_form144_notices, get_ftd_data, get_gov_contracts

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
